difficultyRationale: Tests recognizing a check-then-act race even on a thread-safe collection, and knowing the atomic-compound-operation fix.
explanation: `ConcurrentHashMap` makes each individual call (`containsKey`, `put`) thread-safe on its own, but it does not make a *sequence* of two separate calls atomic as a unit. Both threads can observe `containsKey(key)` return `false` before either one calls `put`, so `computeExpensiveValue` runs twice and one result simply overwrites the other. `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> computeExpensiveValue(k))` performs the check-and-insert as one atomic operation, closing the window entirely.

options.text: Both threads can pass the `containsKey` check before either calls `put`, so `computeExpensiveValue` can run twice for the same key and one result overwrites the other; `cache.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> computeExpensiveValue(k))` performs the check and insert as one atomic operation.
options.explanation: Correct: this is the classic check-then-act race, and `computeIfAbsent` is exactly the atomic compound operation `ConcurrentHashMap` provides to replace it.

options.text: Nothing can go wrong in this or any similar sequence: `ConcurrentHashMap` guarantees that every sequence of separate method calls a caller happens to write one after another — not merely each individual call in isolation — executes as a single atomic, indivisible unit from the perspective of every other thread.
options.explanation: This overstates the guarantee: `ConcurrentHashMap` documents thread safety for its individual operations, not for an arbitrary sequence of separate method calls a caller happens to write one after another.

options.text: The second thread's `put` call throws `ConcurrentModificationException` because the map was already modified by the first thread.
options.explanation: `ConcurrentModificationException` is thrown by fail-fast iterators detecting structural modification during iteration; it is not thrown by concurrent `put` calls on a `ConcurrentHashMap`, which is specifically designed to support concurrent modification without that exception.

options.text: `containsKey` itself is not thread-safe on a `ConcurrentHashMap` and can return an incorrect result even with no race on `put` at all.
options.explanation: `containsKey` on its own is thread-safe and returns an accurate snapshot result; the hazard here is specifically about the gap between two separate, individually-safe calls, not about either call being unsafe in isolation.
